# Learnings

- The Angular landing app lives in `src\CloudSkew.Landing\` and is the workspace used for the CloudSkew landing page rebuild.
- Legacy landing assets are now mirrored into `src\CloudSkew.Landing\public\assets\` so the Angular app can reference the original icons, fonts, thumbnails, and branding locally.
- The landing page preserves the legacy SEO route aliases under `/solutions/:solutionId` and prerenders those routes during the Angular build.
- The landing app now builds as a fully static Angular site via `outputMode: "static"`; deployable files live under `src\CloudSkew.Landing\dist\CloudSkew.Landing\browser\`.
- The landing page deployment workflow runs `npm install` and `npm run build` in `src\CloudSkew.Landing\`, then uploads `src\CloudSkew.Landing\dist\CloudSkew.Landing\browser\` to Azure Static Web Apps; place `staticwebapp.config.json` under `src\CloudSkew.Landing\public\` so Angular copies it to that artifact root.
- The UI app deployment workflow runs `npm install` and `npm run build-testing` in `src\CloudSkew.Ui\`, then uploads `src\CloudSkew.Ui\dist\cloudskew-ui\` to the `cloudskew-ui` Azure Static Web App.
- The UI app now uses an IndexedDB-backed local `APIService` path for anonymous user profiles, diagrams, diagram thumbnails, and diagram templates; print/export image generation still uses the diagram helper API.
- The Angular 21 landing app keeps its legacy NgModule/component file shape by marking declared components with `standalone: false`; prerender route configuration lives in `AppServerModule` via `provideServerRendering(withRoutes(...))`.
- For Angular 21 static output, use `outputMode: "static"` without a separate `prerender` option. Critical CSS inlining is disabled in production because the Angular 21 CSS inliner currently fails in this Node 24 workspace with `document.documentElement?.setAttribute is not a function`.
- The user manual docs app lives in `docs\user-manual\` and uses VuePress 2 RC with npm. CI should run `npm ci` and `npm run docs:build`, then upload `docs\user-manual\.vuepress\dist\` to the `cloudskew-docs` Azure Static Web App; place `staticwebapp.config.json` under `docs\user-manual\.vuepress\public\` so VuePress copies it to the artifact root.
- The blog app lives in `docs\blog\` and uses VuePress 2 RC with npm. CI should run `npm ci` and `npm run docs:build`, then upload `docs\blog\.vuepress\dist\` to the `cloudskew-blog` Azure Static Web App; place `staticwebapp.config.json` under `docs\blog\.vuepress\public\` so VuePress copies it to the artifact root.
- `src\CloudSkew.Ui\` no longer supports the obsolete per-diagram attached document editor; `documentDetails` flow and the Syncfusion rich text editor dependency were removed, while the separate Resource Documentation popups remain.
- The `CloudSkew.Ui` app builds and lints successfully from `src\CloudSkew.Ui\` with `npm run build` and `npm run lint`.
- `src\CloudSkew.Ui\` now uses a single active-diagram model: the My Diagrams sidebar is gone, `/editor/:id` is removed, IndexedDB keeps one active diagram record, create/import confirm before replacing it, and delete resets the current canvas to a blank diagram.
- `src\CloudSkew.Landing\` no longer keeps the obsolete Express Universal scaffold; prerendering uses `src\main.server.ts` and `AppServerModule`, while the old `server.ts`, `tsconfig.server.json`, and broken `run.local.sh` were removed.
- `src\CloudSkew.Ui\` no longer includes the legacy Protractor scaffold; the tracked `e2e\` folder, `ng e2e` target, and Protractor-only devDependencies were removed, so validation there is `npm run build` and `npm run lint`.
- `src\CloudSkew.Ui\` no longer includes the dormant extension sidebar path or unused sanitize/profile resolver artifacts; `extension-grid`, `IExtensionDefinition`, `sanitize-html.pipe.ts`, and `user-profile-resolver.service.ts` were removed, and `SidebarType` now only includes the live palette/create/preference modes.
- `src\CloudSkew.Ui\` now consolidates anonymous local state into `local-persistence.service.ts`: IndexedDB owns the active diagram and persisted preferences, `APIService` only handles remote image/file calls, and the old `session.service.ts` plus `local-api-storage.service.ts` were removed.
- `src\CloudSkew.Ui\` no longer carries any local user-profile model or status bar profile flow; preferences persist as a dedicated IndexedDB record and the active diagram uses a fixed local record key instead of fake user-owned storage.
- `src\CloudSkew.Ui\` no longer stores diagram names in client DTOs; `DiagramDTO` now keeps only `diagramDetails` and `lastUpdatedUTC`, `DiagramImportDTO` keeps only `diagramDetails`, the `diagram-name-editor` control is removed, and exports/downloads use the fixed filename `cloudskew-diagram`.
- `src\CloudSkew.Ui\` removed support-email and MD5-specific client terminology from the active-diagram flow: the support email menu item is gone, the fake diagram helper user id is now treated as an asset container id, and save dedupe tracks serialized diagram state instead of an MD5 hash.
- `src\CloudSkew.Ui\` custom images are now embedded directly in Syncfusion image nodes as `data:image/...;base64,...` sources; the image upload dialog reads valid JPG/PNG files locally and no longer posts custom images to the old public blob API.
- `src\CloudSkew.Ui\` no longer has a left activity bar; CloudSkew branding, import, add/remove symbols, and help/support now live in the top diagram control bar, while the left sidebar stays as the symbol palette.
- `src\CloudSkew.Assets\run-local.ps1` serves `src\CloudSkew.Assets` on `http://localhost:7001`; the UI dev environment intentionally keeps `cdnUrlPrefix` pointed at that local asset endpoint so palette stencils render and can be fetched into the canvas.
- `docs\specs\ui.md` now captures the intended design refresh for the `CloudSkew.Ui` top control bar and bottom status bar, and the supporting review mockups live under `docs\ui-mockups\CloudSkewUiTopControlBar\` and `docs\ui-mockups\CloudSkewUiBottomStatusBar\`.
- `src\CloudSkew.Ui\` now applies the refreshed editor chrome in-app: the top control bar uses grouped dark command-bar styling with styled Angular Material menus, the status bar renders mode/zoom chips, and the UI test suite runs from `src\CloudSkew.Ui\` with `npm test -- --watch=false --browsers=ChromeHeadless`.
- `docs\specs\ui.md` now captures the intended minimal dialog refresh for `CloudSkew.Ui`: keep existing dialog copy unchanged and refine only shell, spacing, typography, button emphasis, and file-input styling; the Angular Material implementation centers dialogs via shared dialog defaults, uses global MDC-based dialog styling in `src\styles.css`, and reference mockups live under `docs\ui-mockups\CloudSkewUiDialogConfirmation\` and `docs\ui-mockups\CloudSkewUiDialogImport\`.
- `docs\specs\ui.md` now captures the intended property-editor refresh for `CloudSkew.Ui`, covering the right-side inspector shell, shared control treatments, and editor-family-specific guidance; the supporting mockups live under `docs\ui-mockups\CloudSkewUiPropertyEditorShell\` and `docs\ui-mockups\CloudSkewUiPropertyEditorVariants\`.
- `src\CloudSkew.Ui\` now applies the documented property-editor refresh in-app: the right rail is widened to `280px`, shared inspector styling lives in `src\styles.css`, property-editor templates expose explicit aria labels for the touched icon-only controls, and a smoke spec exists at `src\app\components\propertiesbar\propertiesbar.component.spec.ts`.
- `src\CloudSkew.Ui\` now carries the fuller property-editor refresh in the live editor templates: section cards replace divider rows, locked editors remain visible but muted, metadata renders as chips, and property toggles use the shared switch-style treatment from `src\styles.css`.
- `docs\specs\ui.md` now captures the simplified `CloudSkew.Ui` sidebar palette refresh: keep the header minimal, avoid family chips, use a plain search field with clear spacing, preserve a dedicated chevron gutter in group headers, and use a quiet vertical-ellipsis documentation action; the supporting mockups live under `docs\ui-mockups\CloudSkewUiSidebarPaletteShell\` and `docs\ui-mockups\CloudSkewUiSidebarPaletteVariants\`.
- `CloudSkew.Ui` now keeps Add/Remove Symbols in the palette header as a compact filter icon between `Symbol palette` and the symbol-count chip, keeps the `libraries enabled` link left-aligned, and removes the top-bar filter button in favor of an amber-outlined delete/import danger zone immediately before the lock/help endcap.
- The top control bar now includes explicit spacer offsets before the Insert group and before the amber danger zone group so command clusters do not crowd the CloudSkew branding block or adjacent output actions; current spacing targets are `24px` desktop and `12px` on narrower widths in app CSS, spec, and the `CloudSkewUiTopControlBar` mockup.
